content.title: Fixed workshop｜Planar bead array layer by layer three-dimensional forming
content.summary: Locking the boundaries of the tabletop and materials in the same workshop, the planar bead array first forms a partial pattern in an irreversible stage, then raises the main three-dimensional structure, adds secondary objects and supporting bases, and finally accepts the complete three-dimensional combination in the same composition.

quick_start.input_format: Object + fixed composition + 4 irreversible production stages + final small movements
quick_start.recommended_input: On the original clay geology workbench, inside the square graphite mold is a completely flat cream-colored contour map; the brass calipers, cobalt blue glazed cups and height sketches are fixed in position; the central ring rises into a volcanic cone, and the adjacent clay is lifted into terraces in countless levels, retaining real indentations, cracks and projections; the dark blue glass only flows into the basin and condenses into a reflective lake. The volcano, terraces, instrument tower and lake are completely located within the original square mold, and the fixed tools are all visible
required_anchors: Lock one bounded work surface and preserve its registration anchors for the full sequence.

Hold the finished assembly in the original composition with the work-surface anchors still visible.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock one bounded work surface and its surrounding registration anchors. Start from a visibly flat or incomplete material state, commit the material to a readable central identity, then add irreversible height, secondary structures and support geometry in countable stages without moving the camera. End only when the finished assembly can be compared directly with the original material footprint in the same composition.

instantiations.concept: On an original ceramic geology bench, a flat cream-clay contour map sits inside a square mold. Without moving the camera, cobalt fault lines appear, one volcanic cone rises, terraced ridges and instrument pylons emerge, and a dark glass lake sets into a completed research diorama while mold corners and tools remain fixed.
